parsed.explanation: This is state-directed targeting of gender-nonconforming people: a 2024 law classifying depictions of transgender people as pornography (up to 4 years, 13 with children), a 2026 'gender reassignment propaganda' ban, and a documented September 2024 wave of detentions including eight transgender people, with reported beatings and coerced charges. A visitor's own image or presence can constitute criminal material. Recourse is absent: no SOGI asylum ground, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, no regional court, police brutality unregistered, prison custody hostile. Death penalty retained in the general system. Severity is tier 2–3 (imprisonment, custodial violence, expulsion) at high frequency with the state's own hand; no credible execution pathway for trans identity itself is documented, keeping this above the 0.05 anchors but near the 0.15 band's floor.

entry_documents.exposure: Foreign documents' treatment undocumented; visitors at LGBT events threatened with expulsion under 'intervention in domestic affairs' (2004). Passport details and photographs collected by police at cruising areas.
entry_documents.interaction: Police data collection converts any police contact into outing and a recorded file.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Eight trans people among 15+ detained in Sept 2024; hooliganism and pornography charges; beatings and coerced charges reported; custody abuse reported; prison placement exposes to speculation, blackmail, staff-encouraged abuse; death penalty retained nationally.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; NGOs note charges are coerced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention escalates to custodial violence with no oversight since hate-crime data unreported since 2015.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Public presence or image of a trans person can be treated as pornographic material; propaganda ban covers representation of transition; venues raided or closed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Applies to visitors' ordinary public existence and any event attendance.

care_services.exposure: Qualified psychological care generally unavailable; no trans-specific facilities documented; care access for visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or continuity-of-care needs would expose the visitor to untrained, hostile institutions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State media equates LGBTI identities with paedophilia and foreign weapons; decree groups 'homosexualism' with necrophilia; security concept centres 'traditional values'; police do not register brutality or investigate motives.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses police sweeps and social violence.

minors_guardians.exposure: Penalties rise to thirteen years where children are involved; an adult travelling with a minor while visibly trans risks aggravated pornography or propaganda charges touching the child.
minors_guardians.interaction: Presence of a minor aggravates criminal exposure rather than mitigating it.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans people open about identity face harassment and physical violence; two trans men raped in 2008 and did not report, expecting no police help; venue raids; owner of a closed gay club later killed.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; police response is the exposure.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Non-reporting is rational; victims have no redress.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No SOGI asylum ground, no partner recognition, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, no regional court appeal, no official hate-crime data since 2015. Whether the 2026 law is in force and how border/hotel document checks treat trans visitors is not established.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin-document questions unresolved, but the structural facts (criminalisation, no relief) govern the extrapolation.

anchor_checks.comparison: Shares religious-adjacent moral criminalisation and state threat-framing, but here the documented worst outcomes are imprisonment, custodial abuse and expulsion rather than a credibly applied capital pathway to execution for trans presentation; hence materially above 0.05.

Very close: statute-driven criminalisation of presentation/image, routine arrests of trans people, beatings in custody, coerced charges, illusory remedies, capital provision retained but not documented as applied to trans cases — near the 0.15 tier's floor.

Both feature morality-law enforcement and media amplification, but 0.25-D's penalties are fines and short terms with courts annulling cases; here sentences reach years, custody abuse is routine, and no court relief is documented, placing this well below 0.25.

0.35-B's detentions end in release without imprisonment and courts formally operate; here detention is frequent, charges are criminal, custody is violent, and remedies consistently fail — clearly below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is a single hostile national system: criminalising statutes (pornography redefinition, propaganda ban) plus police sweeps plus custodial abuse plus zero recourse at any level. Exposure is universal for any trans visitor whose image, documents, or presence draws attention — not limited to event attendees. The state is perpetrator and enabler: it frames trans identity as paedophilic and foreign, its police beat and coerce, and its prisons are unsafe. No protective layer operates anywhere in the journey; the only mitigations are undocumented border practice and the absence of a documented execution pathway for trans identity. This sits at the top of the Severe Risk band.
